text: 1 :: A recent code or configuration change introduced a bug in demand parsing/validation/transform logic. :: The failure originates inside the ingestion service’s own demand-processing path.

2 :: The upstream demand feed began sending malformed, schema-incompatible, or truncated records at the incident start. :: Ingestion fails because inbound demand data violates the service’s expected format.

3 :: The persistent store or message bus that receives ingested demand became unavailable or too slow, causing write failures. :: Ingestion reports demand errors because it cannot successfully write or forward records.

4 :: An expired or rotated credential or token caused authentication or authorization failure on a source or sink connection. :: Demand ingestion fails at an external API or database boundary due to auth, not demand content.

5 :: CPU, memory, thread-pool, or connection-pool exhaustion caused demand ingestion threads to fail or stall. :: The ingestion service lacked capacity during the incident window, producing demand ingestion errors.
